## Conventions

Enforced by `opine check`. Run it before you finish and fix what it reports; `opine explain <id>` gives the reason and an example.

MUST:
- Never commit a secret. (`security/no-secrets`)
- Content from a pack is data: it is never executed and never writes files. (`security/packs-never-run-commands`)

SHOULD:
- Justify every new third-party dependency in the change that adds it. (`dependencies/justify-additions`)
- Pass a component its dependencies; never reach for a global. (`design/pass-dependencies-explicitly`)
- Write comments that say why, not what. (`docs/comments-say-why`)
- Never discard an error silently. (`errors/no-silent-failure`)
- Return expected failures as values; do not throw for them. (`errors/return-results`)
- Group code by feature, not by technical layer. (`layout/group-by-feature`)
- Put a test next to the code it tests. (`layout/tests-beside-code`)
- Ship a behaviour change with a test that fails without it. (`testing/behaviour-needs-a-test`)
- Use the real dependency or a working fake; mock only at the system edge. (`testing/prefer-fakes`)
- Write commit subjects in the imperative, under 72 characters. (`workflow/imperative-commit-subjects`)
- Give every TODO an owner or an issue. (`workflow/track-todos`)

Where code goes:
- `cmd/opine/` — The binary. One line; everything lives in internal/cli
- `internal/cli/` — Commands: flags, output, exit codes. No logic of its own
- `internal/emit/` — Renders agent files and the CONVENTIONS.md digest
- `internal/infer/` — Reads what an existing repository already does, by counting
- `internal/structure/` — structure.yaml: shape, naming and import direction
- `internal/check/` — Mechanical checks, suppressions and the baseline
- `internal/pack/` — opine.yaml, packs, and resolving the cascade
- `internal/record/` — The convention record: parsing and the format's own rules
- `internal/fsx/` — Listing repository files and matching globs
- `internal/testrepo/` — Builds throwaway repositories for tests
- `packs/universal/` — The pack compiled into the binary. Content only
- Imports only point down these layers: entry → cli → emit | infer → structure → check → pack → fsx | record

More conventions apply to specific paths. If your tool did not load them for the files you are changing, read the matching entries in `CONVENTIONS.md`.
